articles.title: Local LLM vs Cloud API: The VRAM Math, Unit Economics, and Routing Architecture
articles.excerpt: Almost nobody should deploy exclusively on local silicon or entirely behind a provider's API key. The functional engineering question is determining which segments of your workload belong on internal…
articles.body: Almost nobody should deploy exclusively on local silicon or entirely behind a provider's API key. The functional engineering question is determining which segments of your workload belong on internal hardware and which justify managed endpoints. Cloud models remain superior at deep multi-step reasoning, massive context processing, and complex tool orchestration. However, modern open-weight releases mean keeping sensitive data offline is no longer a compromise on utility. The architectural decision hinges on three constraints: physical memory limits, token volume break-even points, and regulatory data isolation. Memory Sets the Execution Ceiling Compute ratings dictate generation speed, but available memory dictates whether a model initializes at all.

articles.title: Two Runs Must Agree Before You Freeze a CLI Transcript
articles.excerpt: Freeze a repo's behavior only after two independent runs produce the same transcript. If two runs disagree, you have no baseline, only noise. This article builds a process-boundary harness that measur…
articles.body: Freeze a repo's behavior only after two independent runs produce the same transcript. If two runs disagree, you have no baseline, only noise. This article builds a process-boundary harness that measures that, then guards the smallest safe change. Most refactor baselines live at the function boundary. Someone calls build_report() and snapshots the returned string. That is convenient, and it hides the parts that actually break: exit codes, stderr, files written, and ordering across a whole run. Why the Process Boundary Wins First Functions change signatures freely. A CLI's contract changes slowly and visibly. Users script against exit codes and stdout, not against your internal call graph. A transcript is four things: exit code, stdout, stderr, and the output tree.

articles.body: A limit order. You bought at exactly the price you specified, or even a little cheaper. So far, so good. But there is another line worth checking: what did the exchange charge for that fill? You can get a good price and still pay the taker fee. There is no contradiction. In the comments on my previous article , a reader corrected our explanation: a fill better than the limit can mean that the order took an offer already resting in the book. I agreed. Then I wanted to check the next question: what if the fill is not better, but exactly at the limit? How often do we still pay as takers? For a bot, this is more than a terminology issue. It buys and sells repeatedly.

articles.title: Budget Human Minutes Before You Generate Docs: A Contract-Driven Draft Queue
articles.excerpt: The scarce resource in an AI-assisted documentation pipeline is not model output; it is the reviewer minutes you can actually schedule. Free model access makes drafts nearly costless to produce, so pi…
articles.body: The scarce resource in an AI-assisted documentation pipeline is not model output; it is the reviewer minutes you can actually schedule. Free model access makes drafts nearly costless to produce, so pipelines that optimize generation quality often just create a larger unreviewed backlog. A better control point is a per-section contract that decides, before any generation, whether a section is draftable at all and how many minutes its review will consume. The artifact below turns that contract into a sorted queue and exits non-zero whenever an unowned or over-budget section tries to enter the model lane. 1. What the model may draft, and what stays human The split is not about difficulty; it is about who can be held responsible for the sentence.

articles.title: 'Star Trek' legend and sci-fi luminary Walter Koenig dies at 90
articles.excerpt: The man who portrayed the U.S.S. Enterprise’s Pavel Chekov has left us after a 60-year stage and screen career
articles.body: The " Star Trek " community lost one of its most beloved icons on Sunday, October 25, with the sad passing of Walter Koenig at the age of 90 in his North Hollywood home. Koenig was best known as the U.S.S. Enterprise's Russian navigator Pavel Andreievich Chekov for two seasons on "Star Trek: The Original Series." The popular American actor continued in that role for Paramount's first seven "Star Trek" films, which began in 1979's " Star Trek: The Motion Picture " and ended with 1994's " Star Trek: Generations ." A native of Chicago, Illinois, Marvin Walter Koenig was born on Sept. 14, 1936, to Lithuanian immigrant parents and spent his formative years in New York City.

articles.title: What causes mysterious long delayed radio echoes in Earth's atmosphere?
articles.excerpt: Baffling long radio echo delays have prompted a range of potential explanations, most of which focus on a variety of unexplained natural phenomena occurring in Earth's atmosphere.
articles.body: In 1927, Norwegian civil engineer and amateur radio operator Jørgen Hals made an unusual discovery: while monitoring transmissions from a shortwave radio station in Eindhoven, The Netherlands, he began hearing odd, "delayed" radio echoes, arriving approximately three seconds after the original transmissions, that sometimes accompanied the station's signals. "From where this echo comes I cannot say for the present," Hals wrote of his peculiar discovery, adding that he could "only confirm that I really heard it." Almost a century after Hals' discovery, the exact cause of this unusual phenomenon — known today as long delayed echoes, or LDEs — remains unknown.

articles.body: A new stack of Starlink satellites is now in orbit following an early morning SpaceX launch from California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off at 3:25 a.m. EDT (0725 GMT) on Oct. 27, from from Pad 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base. The rocket delivered the 27 satellites of Starlink Group 15-16 to low Earth orbit (LEO), and successfully executed its first stage booster landing. The mission's booster, B1082, cut its engines and disengaged from Falcon 9's upper stage approximately 2.5 minutes into flight, and adjusted its trajectory for a touchdown on SpaceX's Of Course I Still Love You (OCISLY) droneship in the Pacific Ocean. articles.body: Transformers are a crucial but nearly invisible part of our grid. The devices help efficiently move power across long distances, but they’re complicated and in short supply. And given that their basic design hasn’t changed much for about a century, they could use an upgrade.  As the world races to meet rising electricity demand from EVs, data centers, and more, researchers and companies are looking to modernize transformers. New, solid-state versions could help relieve some of the supply concerns and make sure the grid can handle the growing pressure. Conventional transformers generally rely on huge amounts of specialized steel alloys and miles of copper wire to do their work of transferring electricity between circuits.
